required_actions: Run the Windows Update troubleshooter: Start > Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters, Run next to Windows Update (critical)
Check internet connection: Start > Settings > Network & Internet > Wi-Fi, reconnect if needed
Check for updates again from Settings > Windows Update
Contact the wire transfer company, say you were tricked, ask for a refund (critical)
Call the granddaughter at a number you know is hers; if unreachable try another family member or her friends
Contact the credit card issuer using the number on the back of the card or the issuer's website/app (critical)
Report the charge and ask for a refund
Report the text in the messaging app, or forward to 7726 if no report-junk option
Report to the FTC at ReportFraud.ftc.gov
Do not buy the gift cards or give numbers/photos (critical)
Hang up/stop; verify by contacting the nephew directly (known number); if unreachable, try another family member or his friends
Report to the FTC at ReportFraud.ftc.gov
If already paid: contact the gift card company, ask for money back, keep the card and store receipt
unsupported_claims: "Keep a copy of the gift card and the store receipt" -> page says keep the card itself and the store receipt (and take photos of both), not 'a copy'
reasons: User said his regular phone is off so he cannot be reached; step 2 only says to use a known number, which does not help here and gives no alternative. The FTC family-emergency page says to try another family member or his friends. Gift card keep-advice is slightly misworded.
fix: In step 2 after 'Reach your nephew through a number you already know is his', add: 'If his phone stays off, ask another family member or his friends to check on him.' (source: https://consumer.ftc.gov/consumer-alerts/2023/03/scammers-use-ai-enhance-their-family-emergency-schemes). In the last paragraph replace 'Keep a copy of the gift card and the store receipt.' with 'Keep the card and the store receipt, and take photos of both.'

required_actions: Tap Add at the bottom right
Enter name and an email address or phone number (critical)
